# Glossary of Biological Terms {#sec-glossary}

## A

**Amino acid** -- The building blocks of proteins. There are 20 standard amino acids, each coded by one or more codons.

**AnnData** -- A Python data structure for annotated data matrices, commonly used in single-cell analysis.

**AlphaFold** -- An AI system by DeepMind that predicts protein 3D structure from amino acid sequence.

**ATP** -- Adenosine triphosphate, the primary energy carrier in cells.

## B

**Base pair (bp)** -- Two nucleotides on opposite DNA strands connected by hydrogen bonds. A pairs with T; C pairs with G.

**BioPerl** -- A collection of Perl modules for bioinformatics.

**BioPython** -- A collection of Python modules for bioinformatics.

**BLAST** -- Basic Local Alignment Search Tool. A program for comparing sequences against databases.

## C

**Chromosome** -- A long DNA molecule containing many genes. Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes.

**Clone** -- A DNA fragment inserted into a vector for replication.

**Codon** -- A sequence of three nucleotides that codes for a specific amino acid.

**Complementary DNA (cDNA)** -- DNA synthesized from an RNA template.

**CRISPR** -- A gene-editing tool that can cut DNA at specific locations.

## D

**Deletion** -- A mutation where one or more nucleotides are removed from a sequence.

**Differential expression** -- Genes that are expressed at different levels between conditions.

**DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid)** -- The molecule that carries genetic information. A double helix of four nucleotide bases: A, T, C, G.

## E

**E-value** -- The expected number of matches with a given score that would occur by chance in a database search.

**Exon** -- A segment of DNA that is transcribed into RNA and retained in the mature mRNA.

## F

**FASTA** -- A text-based format for representing nucleotide or protein sequences.

**Frameshift** -- A mutation that shifts the reading frame of a gene.

## G

**Gene** -- A segment of DNA that encodes a functional product (usually a protein).

**GenBank** -- A database of genetic sequences maintained by NCBI.

**Genome** -- The complete set of DNA in an organism.

**GTF/GFF** -- File formats for gene annotation.

## H

**Homology** -- Similarity between sequences due to shared ancestry.

**HSP** -- High-Scoring Pair. A local alignment with a high score in BLAST.

## I

**Indel** -- An insertion or deletion mutation.

**Intron** -- A segment of DNA that is transcribed but removed during RNA processing.

## K

**K-mer** -- A substring of length k, used in sequence analysis and assembly.

## L

**Locus** -- A specific position on a chromosome.

## M

**mRNA** -- Messenger RNA. Carries genetic information from DNA to ribosomes for protein synthesis.

**Mutation** -- A change in the DNA sequence.

## N

**NCBI** -- National Center for Biotechnology Information. Maintains GenBank and other databases.

**Nucleotide** -- The building blocks of DNA and RNA: A, T, C, G (DNA) or A, U, C, G (RNA).

## O

**Open reading frame (ORF)** -- A sequence that could encode a protein (starts with ATG, ends with a stop codon).

## P

**PAM** -- Position-Specific Scoring Matrix. A matrix for comparing sequences.

**PCR** -- Polymerase Chain Reaction. A method for amplifying DNA.

**Phylogenetics** -- The study of evolutionary relationships between organisms.

**Plasmid** -- A small, circular DNA molecule found in bacteria.

**Polymorphism** -- Variation in DNA sequence between individuals.

## Q

**QC** -- Quality Control. Checking data quality before analysis.

## R

**Read** -- A short DNA sequence from a sequencing machine.

**Reference genome** -- A representative genome sequence for an organism.

**Restriction enzyme** -- A protein that cuts DNA at specific sequences.

**RNA (Ribonucleic acid)** -- A molecule similar to DNA, involved in gene expression.

**RNA-seq** -- A method for measuring gene expression by sequencing RNA.

## S

**Scaffold** -- A set of contigs ordered and oriented using additional information.

**Sequence alignment** -- Arranging sequences to identify regions of similarity.

**Single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)** -- A single base change in DNA.

**SRA** -- Sequence Read Archive. A database of raw sequencing data.

## T

**Transcription** -- Copying DNA to RNA.

**Translation** -- Converting mRNA to protein.

**tRNA** -- Transfer RNA. Carries amino acids to ribosomes during translation.

## U

**UniProt** -- A database of protein sequences and annotations.

**UTR** -- Untranslated Region. Parts of mRNA that are not translated.

## V

**Variant** -- A difference in DNA sequence compared to a reference.

**VCF** -- Variant Call Format. A file format for storing genetic variants.

## W

**Whole genome sequencing (WGS)** -- Sequencing an organism's entire genome.

::: {.callout-tip}
## More Terms

For a comprehensive glossary of bioinformatics terms, see the NCBI glossary: [ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/glossary](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/glossary/)
